classes.name: CType

This class encapsulates the construction and storage of the BBj version of
the !CTYPE table. This table is intended to be used for CVS(), INPUTE, and
string masking. This class uses the builtin Java Unicode data to populate
the !CTYPE table. It uses the Unicode category information to determine the
type of a letter. All letters not considered letters, numbers, spaces or
control characters by Unicode are considered "punctuation" for the purposes
of !CTYPE.

methods.name: copyStreams
methods.docu:
This method copies the bytes from one stream to another using `
p_buffer` while ensuring the streams are closed when it returns. It gives
priority first to reporting an Exception on a read() or write(), then on
reporting an Exception when closing the OutputStream, then on reporting
an Exception when closing the InputStream. It obtains the streams for
reading and writing from a `StreamSource`.

It probably looks a lot more complicated than it is. The IE and OE type
parameters are just exceptions that can be thrown from the StreamSource.
In most cases, you probably just want to do something like this:

InputStream is = ...
OutputStream os = ...
Util.copyStreams(new Util.DefaultStreamSource(is, os), null);

The IE and OE types are available if the StreamSource implementation you
pass in can throw other kinds of exceptions (like IOException, for
instance).

**Parameters:**

- `IE` The exception type thrown by
`StreamSource#getInputStream()`
- `OE` The exception type thrown by
`StreamSource#getOutputStream()`.
- `p_source` The `StreamSource` used to obtain the streams.
- `p_buffer` A buffer of desired length. If this argument is `null`,
this method will use a buffer size of `#BUFFER_SIZE`.

**Returns:** The number of bytes copied between the two streams.

classes.name: WeakIdentityHashMap
classes.docu:
WeakIdentityHashMap is a modification of Java1.4.2 source code for
java.lang.WeakHashMap. It has been modified in the following ways
1) it extends AbstractMapB rather than AbstractMap. AbstractMapB
is a copy of AbstractMap except that it is in com.basis.util.common
2) WeakIdentityMap implements the method hashB() which is a direct copy
of java.util.HashMap.hash(). All calls to HashMap.hash() have been
replaced with calls to hashB()
3) NULL_KEY is protected rather than private so that it can be used by
WeakKeyValueIdentityHashMap
4) the method eq(Object x, Object y) requires referenceEquality rather
than referenceEqulity OR ObjectEquality

classes.name: ReflectionProxy
classes.docu:
The class has methods that you can use to create a proxy wrapper around a
class that has the exact same methods as an interface but does not actually
implement the interface. For example, if you instantiate a class that
implements an interface from a different ClassLoader then the class in
question implements all of the correct methods but according to Java does not
actually implement the interface that you want (because of the different
ClassLoader). This class should let you wrap that instance in the interface
recognized by the local ClassLoader. Be careful here, since the reflection
may allow the caller to call methods that they would not normally be allowed
to call.

For simplicities sake I am assuming that the arguments and return values do
not need to be translated, but if it turns out to be necessary then it should
be possible using the interface ClassLoader to check the types.

classes.name: VolatileStringKeyMap
classes.docu:
This class implements a safe map with VolatileString objects as keys.
Inserting a VolatileString key into this map will contribute a reference to
the refcount of the VolatileString. Replacing the value associated with a key
will not change the refcount for the key, and removing a mapping will
decrement the reference count of the internal buffer for that key (as this
map will no longer contain a reference to it).

Internally, this class uses a MapPrivateString, V> to keep the references to
the VolatileString safe.

This map cannot safely be used from multiple threads simultaneously. To use
in multiple threads, use `Collections#synchronizedMap(Map)`.

classes.name: ReadWriteLock
classes.docu:
This class is an implementation of the Read/Write lock design
pattern as described in "Concurrent Programming in Java" by
Doug Lea and also described in "Patterns in Java Volume 1"
by Mark Grand. It allows concurrent read access to an object
but requires exclusive access for write operations.

This class can be used anywhere that read and write access
to an object by multiple threads is going to occur. Basically,
create an instance of ReadWriteLock, call readLock() every time
before performing any read operations in the object, and call
writeLock() when making a change to the object. When the reading
or writing process is complete, call the done() method to let
everyone know that the current thread is done reading or writing.

methods.name: compareTo
methods.docu:
Compares two strings lexicographically.
The comparison is based on the bytes in
the strings. The byte sequence represented by this
BasisString object is compared lexicographically to the
byte sequence represented by the argument string. The result is
a negative integer if this BasisString object
lexicographically precedes the argument string. The result is a
positive integer if this BasisString object lexicographically
follows the argument string. The result is zero if the strings
are equal; compareTo returns 0 exactly when
the `#equals(Object)` method would return true.

This is the definition of lexicographic ordering. If two strings are
different, then either they have different characters at some index
that is a valid index for both strings, or their lengths are different,
or both. If they have different characters at one or more index
positions, let k be the smallest such index; then the string
whose character at position k has the smaller m_buffer, as
determined by using the operator, lexicographically precedes the
other string. In this case, compareTo returns the
difference of the two character values at position k in
the two string -- that is, the m_buffer:

this.charAt(k)-anotherString.charAt(k)

If there is no index position at which they differ, then the shorter
string lexicographically precedes the longer string. In this case,
compareTo returns the difference of the lengths of the
strings -- that is, the m_buffer:

this.length()-anotherString.length()

**Parameters:**

- `p_string` the String to be compared.

**Returns:** the m_buffer 0 if the argument string is equal to
this string; a m_buffer less than 0 if this string
is lexicographically less than the string argument; and a
m_buffer greater than 0 if this string is
lexicographically greater than the string argument.

classes.docu:
Single-byte character set implementations for ConstString toUpperCase and
toLowerCase. In this environment, there is a 1:1 relationship between bytes
and characters. We optimize these conversions by building fast lookup tables
for all 256 possible uppercase and lowercase conversions. Each conversion
process has up to three successive levels. Level 1 determines whether a
conversion is necessary, or if we can just return the original string. Level
2 attempts to perform the entire conversion in-place within a byte[] array.
Level 3 (extremely rarely required) is used for conversions that generate a
result string longer than the original string. It uses a
ByteArrayOutputStream to accommodate the variable length result, with a hack
to avoid making an extra copy of the final byte array.

methods.name: keySet
methods.docu:
Returns a Set view of the keys contained in this map. The Set is
backed by the map, so changes to the map are reflected in the Set,
and vice-versa. (If the map is modified while an iteration over
the Set is in progress, the results of the iteration are undefined.)
The Set supports element removal, which removes the corresponding entry
from the map, via the Iterator.remove, Set.remove, removeAll
retainAll, and clear operations. It does not support the add or
addAll operations.

This implementation returns a Set that subclasses
AbstractSet. The subclass's iterator method returns a "wrapper
object" over this map's entrySet() iterator. The size method delegates
to this map's size method and the contains method delegates to this
map's containsKey method.

The Set is created the first time this method is called,
and returned in response to all subsequent calls. No synchronization
is performed, so there is a slight chance that multiple calls to this
method will not all return the same Set.

**Returns:** a Set view of the keys contained in this map.

methods.name: values
methods.docu:
Returns a collection view of the values contained in this map. The
collection is backed by the map, so changes to the map are reflected in
the collection, and vice-versa. (If the map is modified while an
iteration over the collection is in progress, the results of the
iteration are undefined.) The collection supports element removal,
which removes the corresponding entry from the map, via the
Iterator.remove, Collection.remove,
removeAll, retainAll and clear operations.
It does not support the add or addAll operations.

This implementation returns a collection that subclasses abstract
collection. The subclass's iterator method returns a "wrapper object"
over this map's entrySet() iterator. The size method
delegates to this map's size method and the contains method delegates
to this map's containsValue method.

The collection is created the first time this method is called, and
returned in response to all subsequent calls. No synchronization is
performed, so there is a slight chance that multiple calls to this
method will not all return the same Collection.

**Returns:** a collection view of the values contained in this map.

methods.name: entrySet
methods.docu:

to the map are reflected in the set, and vice-versa. (If the map is
modified while an iteration over the set is in progress, the results of
the iteration are undefined.) The set supports element removal, which
removes the corresponding entry from the map, via the
Iterator.remove, Set.remove, removeAll,
retainAll and clear operations. It does not support

methods.name: equals
methods.docu:
Compares the specified object with this map for equality. Returns
true if the given object is also a map and the two maps
represent the same mappings. More formally, two maps t1 and
t2 represent the same mappings if
t1.keySet().equals(t2.keySet()) and for every key k
in t1.keySet(), (t1.get(k)==null ? t2.get(k)==null :
t1.get(k).equals(t2.get(k))) . This ensures that the
equals method works properly across different implementations
of the map interface.

This implementation first checks if the specified object is this map;
if so it returns true. Then, it checks if the specified
object is a map whose size is identical to the size of this set; if
not, it it returns false. If so, it iterates over this map's
entrySet collection, and checks that the specified map
contains each mapping that this map contains. If the specified map
fails to contain such a mapping, false is returned. If the
iteration completes, true is returned.

**Parameters:**

- `o` object to be compared for equality with this map.

**Returns:** true if the specified object is equal to this map.

methods.name: hashCode
methods.docu:
Returns the hash code value for this map. The hash code of a map is
defined to be the sum of the hash codes of each entry in the map's
entrySet() view. This ensures that t1.equals(t2)
implies that t1.hashCode()==t2.hashCode() for any two maps
t1 and t2, as required by the general contract of
Object.hashCode.

This implementation iterates over entrySet(), calling
hashCode on each element (entry) in the Collection, and adding
up the results.

**Returns:** the hash code value for this map.

methods.name: toString
methods.docu:
Returns a string representation of this map. The string representation
consists of a list of key-value mappings in the order returned by the
map's entrySet view's iterator, enclosed in braces
("{}"). Adjacent mappings are separated by the characters
", " (comma and space). Each key-value mapping is rendered as
the key followed by an equals sign ("=") followed by the
associated value. Keys and values are converted to strings as by
String.valueOf(Object).

This implementation creates an empty string buffer, appends a left
brace, and iterates over the map's entrySet view, appending
the string representation of each map.entry in turn. After
appending each entry except the last, the string ", " is
appended. Finally a right brace is appended. A string is obtained
from the stringbuffer, and returned.

**Returns:** a String representation of this map.

to java.lang.String except that

classes.docu:
TODO: The com.basis.nb code was removed from SVN BBj trunk in 2023, but this
class may be useful in the future for implementing breakpoints in the
WinConsole, or a future full-screen editor in the SysConsole or BBj
debugger. Hang on to this for the time being, even though NB is gone.

Class which manages storage and retrieval of breakpoints for the
NetBeans-based BBj IDE Debugger. Static methods are provided to find
and open breakpoint files by passing in the path/filename as a String,
or to save breakpoints to a breakpoint file by passing in the path/
filename and an array of breakpoint line numbers.

This class is subclassed by the SourceEditorBreakpointMgr class in
com.basis.nb.bbj.editor, which handles storage and retrieval of breakpoints
for the IDE Source Editor.

NOTE: This class is part of the persistent breakpoint scheme implemented
for BBj 2.01, which I hope will someday disappear in favor of a more
tightly integrated with NetBeans breakpoint serialization scheme.
There were two options for implementing breakpoints in both the
IDE's Source Editor and its Debugger:

1) Use the built-in NetBeans system, where breakpoints are tracked
by the LineSet class and are serialized to disk along with all other
properties and settings. This is the best long term solution for
several reasons, but it would have required extensive changes to
the Debugger.

2) Make more superficial changes to the Source Editor and continue
to use the LineAttributeSet scheme currently employed by the
Debugger. This was the only solution that could be implemented
in time for the release of BBj version 2.01.

Inserting a VolatileString key into this map will contribute a reference to
the refcount of the VolatileString. Replacing the value associated with a key
will not change the refcount for the key, and removing a mapping will
decrement the reference count of the internal buffer for that key (as this
map will no longer contain a reference to it).

Internally, this class uses a MapPrivateString, V> to keep the references to
the VolatileString safe.

This map cannot safely be used from multiple threads simultaneously. To use
in multiple threads, use `Collections#synchronizedMap(Map)`.

backed by the map, so changes to the map are reflected in the set, and

progress (except through the iterator's own remove operation),
the results of the iteration are undefined. The set supports element
removal, which removes the corresponding mapping from the map, via the
Iterator.remove, Set.remove, removeAll,
retainAll, and clear operations. It does not support
the add or addAll operations.

iterator's own remove operation), the results of the iteration
are undefined. The collection supports element removal, which removes the
corresponding mapping from the map, via the Iterator.remove,

methods.name: keySet
methods.docu:
Returns a `Set` view of the keys contained in this map. The set is
backed by the map, so changes to the map are reflected in the set, and
vice-versa. If the map is modified while an iteration over the set is in
progress (except through the iterator's own remove operation),
the results of the iteration are undefined. The set supports element
removal, which removes the corresponding mapping from the map, via the
Iterator.remove, Set.remove, removeAll,
retainAll, and clear operations. It does not support
the add or addAll operations.

in the collection, and vice-versa. If the map is modified while an
iteration over the collection is in progress (except through the
iterator's own remove operation), the results of the iteration
are undefined. The collection supports element removal, which removes the
corresponding mapping from the map, via the Iterator.remove,
Collection.remove, removeAll, retainAll and

addAll operations.

element removal, which removes the corresponding mapping from the map,
